---
title: Tagging Tokens
description: Adding annotations to tokens via regex, predicate, text-level matching, or chat-template roles.
llms-description: tag_by_regex / tag_by_text_regex / tag_by_predicate / tag_chat_roles produce TokenAnnotation entries; create_span_from_tag converts a tag into a Span.
---

INIF's tagging helpers are thin wrappers around `Sample.annotate` /
`Sample.annotate_positions`. They handle the common cases — regex over
token strings, regex over the *concatenated* text (so multi-token matches
work), Python predicates, chat-template roles, and special tokens — without
making you reach for the underlying methods.

All helpers add [`TokenAnnotation`](../concepts/annotations.qmd) entries
unless otherwise noted; per-name auto-merge applies, so calling the same
helper twice with the same name extends the existing record rather than
creating a duplicate.

## Regex over token strings

Tag every token whose string matches a regex.

``` python
from inif import tag_by_regex, tag_by_regex_all

tag_by_regex(sample, r"^\d+$", "number")          # one sample
tag_by_regex_all(doc, r"^\d+$", "number")         # all samples in a doc
```

For multiple patterns in a single token pass — much faster than calling the
single-pattern helper N times:

``` python
from inif import tag_by_regexes, tag_by_regexes_all

tag_by_regexes_all(doc, [
    (r"^\d+$",        "number"),
    (r"^[A-Z]+$",     "uppercase"),
    (r"\.$",          "sentence_end"),
])
```

### Sequence refs

When the document has sequence refs and you pass `sequences=`, the regex
sees the *expanded* view. If a match falls inside a ref, that ref is
materialized in place — only in the sample where the match landed, only
that one ref. Other refs and other samples are left untouched.

``` python
tag_by_regex(sample, r"\bParis\b", "city", sequences=doc.sequences)
```

The `_all` variants forward `doc.sequences` automatically.

## Regex over concatenated text

`tag_by_regex` only sees one token at a time, so it can't match patterns
that span token boundaries (e.g. `"Eiffel"` split by BPE into
`[" E", "iff", "el"]`). For those, use `tag_by_text_regex`, which joins
all token strings, runs the regex on the joined text, then maps character
spans back to token indices.

``` python
from inif import tag_by_text_regex, tag_by_text_regex_all, TextTagMode

tag_by_text_regex(sample, r"Paris", "city")                       # default: ALL
tag_by_text_regex(sample, r"\d+\.\d+", "decimal", TextTagMode.FIRST)
tag_by_text_regex_all(doc, r"\d{4}", "year")
```

`TextTagMode` controls which tokens of a multi-token match get tagged:

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `ALL` (default) | Tag every token overlapping the match. |
| `FIRST` | Tag only the first token of each match. |
| `LAST` | Tag only the last token of each match. |

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
#### Sequence refs are not expanded here

`tag_by_text_regex` operates directly on `sample.tokens`. To match inside
refs, expand first (`sample.materialize_position` or
`sample.get_expanded_tokens`) and run the helper on the expanded view.
This matches the trade-off the function makes for performance — the
character-offset map is rebuilt per call and would have to walk every ref
otherwise.
:::

## Predicate-based tagging

When you need full Python expressivity:

``` python
from inif import tag_by_predicate, tag_by_predicates, tag_by_predicates_all

tag_by_predicate(sample, lambda t: t.id > 50_000, "rare")

tag_by_predicates_all(doc, [
    (lambda t: t.id > 50_000,                                   "rare"),
    (lambda t: t.token is not None and t.token.startswith(" "), "leading_space"),
])
```

Predicates receive the `Token` object (not just the string), so you can
filter by id, presence of extras, etc. Same sequence-ref handling as the
regex helpers.

## Chat roles

`tag_chat_roles` annotates each token with the role of its enclosing chat
message — `system`, `user`, `assistant` — using character-span matching
against `tokenizer.apply_chat_template`. Delimiters and template-generated
content get tagged `template`.

``` python
from inif import tag_chat_roles_doc

messages_per_sample = [
    [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "..."}],
    ...
]
tag_chat_roles_doc(doc, messages_per_sample, tokenizer)
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="minimal"}
#### Run after dedup

`tag_chat_roles` writes annotations to the *current* `sample.tokens`. Run
sequence deduplication first if you want to (so the annotations don't
prevent collapse), then tag — that order is what the converters use by
default.

Some tokenizers (notably Qwen's, which replaces U+2028 with U+FFFD) are
lossy and won't round-trip from per-token decode back to the formatted
template string. Role tagging is a no-op for those samples rather than
raising.
:::

For a single sample, call `tag_chat_roles(sample, messages, tokenizer,
sequences=doc.sequences)` directly.

## Generated-output tagging

The Inspect AI and evaleval converters add a `generated` annotation
(`metadata={"source": "converter"}`) covering the last assistant
message — the model's actual response. You normally don't need to call this
yourself; it's controlled via `tag_generated=True` (the default) on the
converter entry points. See [`from_eval_log`](../converters/inspect_ai.qmd)
and [`from_instance_records`](../converters/evaleval.qmd) for the option.

## Special tokens

Tag every special token (BOS, EOS, etc.) discovered via the tokenizer's
`all_special_ids`:

``` python
from inif import tag_special_tokens

tag_special_tokens(sample, tokenizer)              # tag = "special"
tag_special_tokens(sample, tokenizer, "delimiter") # custom name
```

## Position tagging

If you already know the positions, skip the matching helpers and tag
directly:

``` python
from inif import tag_positions

tag_positions(sample, [3, 5, 7], "manual")
```

## Removing tags

``` python
from inif import remove_tag, remove_tag_all

remove_tag(sample, "manual")        # one sample
remove_tag_all(doc, "manual")       # whole document
```

Both remove every annotation matching the name; metadata-distinguished
duplicates are dropped together.

## Spans from tags

To convert an annotation into a [Span](../concepts/annotations.qmd#span)
(for tooling that consumes spans):

``` python
from inif import create_span_from_tag

span = create_span_from_tag(sample, "city", "answer_span")
```

The created span carries the original tag in its `tags` list and the
flattened position list across every range carrying that name.

## Pattern compilation

Precompile patterns when you re-use them many times:

``` python
import re
from inif import tag_by_regexes_all

NUMBER  = re.compile(r"^\d+$")
INITIAL = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]\.")

tag_by_regexes_all(doc, [(NUMBER, "number"), (INITIAL, "initial")])
```

Pre-compiled `re.Pattern` and bare strings can be mixed freely.
